mcpSupport: MCP can read this help and inspect script effects on traffic it has access to. It cannot read or edit script source, test scripts, or enable them. Use Automation → Scripts for those actions.

sections.title: Write and enable a script
paragraphs: Use scripts for conditional changes, JSON transformations, local responses, or logic shared between a request and its response. Rules handle fixed header and text replacements.
Save draft keeps your work. Save & enable applies it to new requests; Save & apply updates an enabled script. Unsaved edits and failed builds leave the applied script unchanged.

Pause script stops selecting new requests. Requests already in progress keep the version they started with. Scripts run on traffic received by the proxy; direct Composer sends and imported captures do not run scripts.
Export synchronous handlers and import helpers and types from transmog:api. Browser and Node APIs, network access, files, and timers are unavailable. Handlers cannot return promises.
If the applied script becomes unavailable, matching requests can fail. Choose Retry applied script, apply a fix, or Pause script.

sections.title: Callbacks, decisions and permissions
paragraphs: Every callback receives the request, parameters, state, and context. The table shows its additional inputs and allowed decisions. These inputs are read-only.

Return a decision with helpers such as pass(), edit(), and respondJson(). Combine related header, status, and body changes in one edit. Empty bytes clear a complete body. Streaming callbacks also support forward(), emit() and needMore().

Enable the capabilities your changes need. List edited header names in Writable headers; Transmog manages Host, Content-Length, Content-Encoding, Transfer-Encoding, and connection headers. Sensitive values are hidden unless Read sensitive headers is enabled. Header helpers throw when a requested value is hidden.

Method and URL changes need Rewrite request method and URL. A different origin also needs Allow cross-origin URL changes. URLs must be absolute HTTP(S), without credentials or fragments. Status changes need Change response status and accept 200–599. Local responses need Return responses or select assets; abort needs Abort requests.
Errors or unpermitted edits in request/response callbacks fail the request. Once response headers reach the client, failures end the stream. Errors in onCompleted and onFailed become diagnostics.

phases.decisions: Continue; forward or replace a prefix; wait for input; abort. Header/status edits only during initial inspection

sections.title: Filters, buffering and limits
paragraphs: Host and method filters match exactly, ignoring case. The path-prefix filter is case-sensitive. Blank filters match all. Filters select a script before onRequestHead; URL rewrites do not remove later callbacks.

Body callbacks need Read bounded bodies; replacements also need Replace bodies. Response body filters apply to both complete-body and streaming callbacks. HEAD and bodyless statuses (1xx, 204, 205, 304) skip response body callbacks. Blank filters match all; local response bodies are excluded unless included.
Complete-body callbacks hold the message headers until processing finishes, even when returning pass(). Streaming sends headers promptly unless initial inspection or another body stage holds them.

By default, complete bodies and pending input windows are limited to 1 MiB; replacement output to 1 MiB per callback. A streaming body can be larger as input is consumed; proxy-wide content limits still apply. Callbacks have 100 ms and a 64 MiB heap. Limits during message processing fail the request.

sections.title: Stream or wait for response bytes
paragraphs: Export onResponseBody for whole-body edits or headers that depend on the full body; it buffers automatically. Export onResponseChunk to process bytes as they arrive. If both are exported, onResponseBody is the default.

Select a mode per response with { ...pass(), body: "stream" } from onResponseHead. "buffer" requires onResponseBody; "stream" requires onResponseChunk; "skip" bypasses both. Filters and permissions still apply.

event.bytes is the pending decoded input. pass() forwards it all. forward(consumed) forwards an unchanged prefix without body-write permission. emit(bytes) replaces it all; emit(bytes, { consumed }) replaces that input prefix. Both prefix operations retain the rest; consumed counts input bytes and must be positive for nonempty input.

needMore() queues input until more bytes arrive or EOF. When event.end is true, consume the remaining input; waiting at EOF or a full pending queue fails. EOF stays true while retained bytes are consumed. A streamed body receives EOF on normal completion, including when empty.

Chunk boundaries can split text, UTF-8 characters or records. replaceTextChunk(event, "before", "after") handles split literal matches and preserves Content-Type; it needs Replace bodies. For record processing, use needMore() to wait and forward() or emit() to consume a complete record.

To hold headers for initial inspection, return deferResponseHeaders() from onResponseHead. It selects streaming. needMore() keeps headers held; forwarding or replacing input releases this script’s hold. Header/status edits are allowed only while event.canEditHeaders is true; later edits fail even if another stage still buffers. Header inspection has a finite network-wait budget.

Selecting a body callback removes the original Content-Length. Before sending headers, Transmog sets the final encoded length when known and permitted by HTTP; unknown-length output streams without it. Any complete-body stage holds the combined response, including output from streaming scripts.
For long streams, summarize findings in onCompleted. Retained chunk findings and diagnostics are bounded per request; omissions are reported.

sections.title: Parameters and request state
paragraphs: Declare text, boolean, or integer parameters in Filters, capabilities, and parameters; read them through event.parameters. They are saved with the script, so do not use them for secrets.
Use event.state to carry this script’s JSON values between callbacks for one request. Returning state replaces it; omitting state keeps it. Module globals are shared across requests.
Use event.context.elapsedMs for durations and event.context.nowUnixMs for timestamps. event.context.source is proxy for proxy traffic and sandbox for tests.

sections.title: Use API helpers
paragraphs: Import helpers by name, for example import { utf8Decode } from "transmog:api". A namespace import (import * as api from "transmog:api") offers completion as you type. Open Full transmog:api namespace for signatures and types.

pass() makes no message edits; edit() changes a message. setHeader, appendHeader, and removeHeader build header operations. headerText and headerValues return all matching values, including duplicates. requestUrl and the query helpers work with URLs and query pairs.
utf8Encode/utf8Decode convert between text and bytes. UTF-8 decoding rejects invalid bytes by default. base64Encode/base64Decode convert bytes and padded Base64.

readText and readJson read UTF-8 bodies. replaceText, replaceJson, and replaceForm update the body and Content-Type together: enable Replace bodies and allow content-type in Writable headers. readForm/replaceForm support URL-encoded forms, including repeated fields; they do not support multipart forms.
Cookie helpers preserve repeated Cookie pairs and separate Set-Cookie fields. Cookie values are not URL-decoded. Use null for flag attributes such as Secure.
respondText and respondJson return a local response. respondAsset("id@revision") selects an available saved response at onRequestHead only.

sections.title: Logs, annotations and failures
paragraphs: Use console.log, debug, info, warn, error, or trace to inspect execution. Log individual fields: objects appear as labels rather than expanded values.
Open Developer details in test results or Script findings for logs, exceptions, and call frames. Selecting a frame shows the code that ran, preserving your draft.

Annotations add notes to saved traffic and need Add saved traffic annotations. Diagnostics and console output are temporary and are not saved with traffic. Avoid logging credentials or other sensitive content.
onFailed receives event.failure, one of the categories below, without the underlying error message.

sections.title: Debug a script
paragraphs: Choose Open debugger in Automation → Scripts or Settings → Extensions, or toggle it with F12. After the first open, the app toolbar keeps a Debugger shortcut until you quit. Browse saved scripts and installed extension files without activating them. Click beside a line number to toggle a breakpoint, or right-click for a condition. A filled red circle is bound; an outline is pending.

While the workspace is open, normal script and visualizer workers honor breakpoints and debugger statements. Dock it beside Traffic or move it to a separate window. Closing continues paused work and detaches; saved breakpoints return next time.

Continue: F8 or Ctrl+\ (also F5). Step over: F10. Step into: F11. Step out: Shift+F11. Stop: Shift+F5. Hover or focus toolbar icons for their shortcuts. Switch between mapped TypeScript and running JavaScript when a source map is available.

Console commands run JavaScript in the selected paused frame or an idle worker global context, and can change its state. Scope inspection does not execute getters. Conditions reject side effects; a failed condition pauses with an explanation.
Transmog suspends dependent execution deadlines while debugging blocks a worker. Cancellation remains available. Remote client and server timeouts still apply.

Debug test runs the current draft and callback or scenario input in a fresh worker, paused before its first user statement. Restart reruns the test with the current draft and input without applying them to traffic. Stop aborts selected work. Closing, including F12 or Continue and detach, continues paused work and detaches all workers.

sections.title: Test in the sandbox
paragraphs: Single callback runs only the selected handler, starting with empty state. It bypasses the request and body filters. Use it to check a callback’s returned changes.

Exchange scenario tests filters, request/response callbacks, and carried state together. A pass means no script or processing errors. Inspect which callbacks ran and the resulting messages to confirm your changes. Failed streams retain output produced before the failure. A simulated upstream failure can still pass.

Neither mode sends traffic or enables the script. Tests use the draft’s capabilities and parameters, but do not verify network behavior or resolve saved response assets. Supply decoded body fixtures without Content-Encoding. Confirm the result with matching proxy traffic.

To test split input, enter response chunk byte counts; any remaining bytes form the last chunk. Byte counts can split UTF-8 characters. Chunk delays are simulated; their total must fit the second half of the scenario duration. Results show header-release time and a bounded callback timeline. Developer details includes earlier chunk logs and diagnostics; phase evidence records the last callback. Single callback tests let you set EOF and simulate held headers.

sections.title: Complete examples
paragraphs: Each example lists its required settings. Exploratory samples start with changes switched off; focused examples apply the change shown. Set filters and capabilities before enabling a script.

examples.title: Explore the API without changing traffic
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. All switches start false. Enable one switch and its listed capabilities to try a change. For timing, enable shouldRememberRequest and shouldAnnotate, then run an Exchange scenario.

examples.title: Body helpers: text, JSON, forms and raw bytes
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Enable Read bounded bodies. Request body media types: text/plain, application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Response body media types: text/plain, application/json. Body callbacks buffer matching messages even with all switches off. Each replacement lists its required capabilities in the comments.

examples.title: Rewrite a header
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Writable headers: user-agent.

examples.title: Transform a JSON response
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Response body media types: application/json. Enable Read bounded bodies and Replace bodies. Writable headers: content-type.

examples.title: Return a local response
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Path-prefix filter: /fixture. Enable Return responses or select assets.

examples.title: Correlate a request and its completion
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Enable Add saved traffic annotations. Test with Exchange scenario or matching proxy traffic.

examples.title: Streaming text replacement
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Response body media types: text/plain. Enable Read bounded bodies. To try the change, enable Replace bodies and set shouldApplySampleChange to true. Headers are sent promptly; partial matches are queued automatically.

examples.title: Queue complete lines before processing
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Response body media types: text/plain. Enable Read bounded bodies. Set shouldQueueCompleteLines to true to forward complete lines unchanged. To also replace text, set shouldApplySampleChange to true and enable Replace bodies; it queues lines automatically. Use UTF-8 input; try before followed by a newline, with chunk byte counts 2, 4, 1.

examples.title: Inspect initial bytes before releasing headers
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Response body media types: text/plain. Enable Read bounded bodies. Writable headers: x-sample-prefix. Set shouldInspectInitialBytes to true to wait for four bytes (or EOF) and record their Base64 value in a header.
